summary: This resolves the PR79 merge conflict for the already-approved DDL pre-flight authorization gate: the only substantive conflict-resolution change is renumbering the new protocol article from A15 to A16 to avoid colliding with the pre-existing A15_hold_for_owner_signoff article, with MASTER_INDEX.yaml's cross-reference updated to match; the core deliverable (scripts/ddl_authorization_check.py, its task-gateway.py cmd_start() integration, and its 28-case test suite) is unchanged in substance from the prior approved content. Verified independently rather than trusting the self-report: PROTOCOL_OWNER_AI.yaml and MASTER_INDEX.yaml both parse as valid YAML with no duplicate article IDs, both Python files compile, and all 28 tests in tests/test_ddl_authorization_check.py pass. The gate itself is architecturally sound -- a dispatch-time regex/keyword scan chained into cmd_start() immediately after tight_task_validation.py using the identical run()/json.loads()/fail() rejection pattern already used elsewhere in that file, fails closed on any DDL keyword or DDL-capable Supabase MCP tool name absent a PRE-APPROVED-LIVE-DDL citation, and verifies KE-id/decision-file citations actually exist on disk rather than trusting shape alone. No .github/workflows/** files are touched, and no path in this diff matches the tier2 triggers (migrations/, schema.sql, *.sql, auth/, permission/payment/billing/rls/security, .env) or a heavy-deletion diff, consistent with the pre-assigned tier1 classification.
issues: Documented (not hidden) limitation: this is a dispatch-time text scan of the prompt-file, not a runtime interceptor of the actual MCP tool call -- a worker whose prompt says nothing about DDL but decides mid-task to call apply_migration/execute_sql/merge_branch anyway is not caught.

Documented (not hidden) limitation: the dated-free-text-note approval path (as opposed to a KE-id/decision-file citation) has no existence check, so a plausible-sounding fabricated free-text note would still pass; low severity since a KE-id/decision-file citation is the preferred path and is existence-checked.
